newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung unveils "fully working" 1GB DRAM die.
newsitem.headline: Samsung unveils "fully working" 1GB DRAM die.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co has successfully developed a "fully working die" for the one-gigabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips, company president Lee Yoon-woo said on Monday.
"We are the world's first to succeed in developing the fully working die," Lee told a news conference. It is the last step before making an engineering sample, he said.
Samsung Electronics, flagship of Samsung Group, announced the development of a circuit design for the chip in December 1995.
Lee said his company would soon start working on engineering samples.
Lee said the one-gigabit DRAM chips, each having four times the memory capability of a 256-megabit chip, were expected to be used commercially in 2002 or 2003.
The world's leading DRAM makers have said sample shipments of one-gigabit DRAMs will start as early as 1998. Samsung did not give a timetable for its sample shipments.
"An important thing is that we are now ready to make samples in the very near future," said Lee.
He also said the technology accumulated in the development of the "fully working die" would help the company cut production costs for other chips.
